text:
dan_support: Customer Acme Health (private deployment, eu-west-1) opened an escalation — intermittent TLS handshake failures against our inference control plane + streaming resets. They see 502/504s and short TLS sessions where client reports 'tls: unexpected message'. They use an outbound proxy that does TLS inspection and a split-horizon DNS for internal -> control-plane IPs. Can infra/network triage?

kevin_se: Thanks, can you paste minimal repro + one tcpdump/openssl trace? Also confirm whether this hits hosted or private control-plane IPs (are they pointing to our public endpoint or internal vip?).

dan_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) From private instance in their VPC: curl https://inference.redwood-prod.internal/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer **redacted**' --stream 2) They see partial response then TLS layer fails and connection RSTs.

kevin_se: Ok please ask for these checks:
- dig +short inference.redwood-prod.internal (from instance)
- openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.redwood-prod.internal -showcerts
- tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap 'tcp port 443' for a failed run

sarah_ops: Also have them run curl -v --resolve inference.redwood-prod.internal:<ip> to force name -> ip mapping, in case split-horizon is returning internal IPs. If outbound proxy rewrites SNI to something else that would break cert validation.

maria_network: Quick guess: outbound proxy doing TLS MITM (corporate TLS inspection) or NAT instance/NACL blocking high source ephemeral ports on return path. We saw a customer recently with a NACL that only allowed 1024-49151 and dropped >49152 return, which broke long-lived streaming.

dan_support: They supplied outputs:

```
# dig output
$ dig +short inference.redwood-prod.internal @127.0.0.53
10.2.5.18

# openssl s_client
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.2.5.18:443 -servername inference.redwood-prod.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-proxy.local
   i:/CN/Enterprise-Proxy-CA
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 1024 bytes and written 512 bytes
write:errno=104
```

# tcpdump snippet (filtered)
$ tcpdump -nn -r trace.pcap 'tcp port 443' | head -n 12
10.2.5.18.443 > 10.2.7.34.51760: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 229, length 511
10.2.7.34.51760 > 10.2.5.18.443: Flags [.], ack 512, win 502, length 0
10.2.5.18.443 > 10.2.7.34.51760: Flags [R], seq 789, win 0, length 0
```

kevin_se: Interesting — cert CN shows a corporate proxy cert (redwood-proxy.local). That explains the verify error and the CN mismatch. The RST after a few hundred bytes suggests the proxy or a firewall is terminating streams.

maria_network: Can we confirm NACL/SG state? Ask customer to run these and paste output:
```
# check SGs on instance
curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/security-groups

# check NACL rules (we gave cli snippet they can run from management host):
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filter Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxx --query 'NetworkAcls[*].Entries' --output json
```

infra_oncall: Also ask them to tcpdump on the NAT device or proxy so we can see if RST originates from their proxy (src ip) or from path (RST with firewall signature). If RST source ip is proxy, then proxy config (idle timeout / max segment) may be killing long streams or doing a per-request policy.

dan_support: Customer returned NACL/Security group snippet: they have an explicit DENY rule that drops ephemeral-range: source ports >49152 on return. Paste (redacted):

```
NACL: rule 100: outbound ALLOW tcp 443 0.0.0.0/0
NACL: rule 110: inbound DENY tcp 49152-65535 0.0.0.0/0 (explicit deny)
```

maria_network: That inbound deny is the culprit for streaming: our server uses high source ports for the server->client leg for long-lived connections (some NATs rewrite). When return packets land on instance they have source port in ephemeral range and inbound NACL denies. That leads to RSTs. The workaround is to add inbound allow for 49152-65535 or broaden rules.

kevin_se: For SNI/cert issue: they also have TLS inspection that replaces certs. Two action items:
- Short term: have customer add NACL inbound allow for ephemeral range (49152-65535) or remove the explicit deny.
- Medium term: disable SNI rewrite / TLS interception for traffic to inference.redwood-prod.internal or add our proxy CA to their trust store and allow passthrough for that hostname.

dan_support: I patched a KB and suggested steps to customer with commands:
```
# To test without proxy, on instance (if allowed):
curl -v --noproxy '*' --resolve inference.redwood-prod.internal:10.2.5.18 https://inference.redwood-prod.internal/v1/stream

# To confirm port allowlist change worked:
# after NACL change, rerun tcpdump and expect no RSTs
tcpdump -nn -s0 'tcp port 443' | grep RST
```

deploy-bot: deployment/infra-update requested by @maria_network: opened ticket NET-8912 to relax inbound NACL for vpc-xxxx. ETA 3h. :thumbsup:

infra_oncall: I'll keep an eye on NET-8912 and coordinate with customer network team. If they can't change NACL, we can propose using a NAT gateway managed path that preserves port mapping (but customer prefers their own NAT/proxy).

dan_support: Customer confirmed after NACL rule removal the streams stay up and TLS handshake shows our cert chain (no proxy CN). They will still audit proxy config to avoid SNI rewrite for our hostnames. Closing loop and asking CS to update the support ticket with NET-8912 and customer's remediation notes. :white_check_mark:
